memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Isaac was old and his eyes were so weak that he could no longer see, he called for Esau his older son and said to him, 'My son.' 'Here I am,' he answered. Isaac said, 'I am now an old man and don't know the day of my death. Now then, get your equipment—your quiver and bow—and go out to the open country to hunt some wild game for me. Prepare me the kind of tasty food I like and bring it to me to eat, so that I may give you my blessing before I die.'" - Gen 27:1-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Isaac is old and blind, sensing the end of his life. So he prepares to give the family blessing — but he calls for Esau, his favourite, the son of his taste for wild game. There is a problem here that runs deeper than food. Years earlier, God had plainly said that "the older will serve the younger" (Gen 25:23). The blessing was meant for Jacob. Yet Isaac, guided by his preferences rather than God's revealed word, sets out to bless Esau instead.

This is a quiet but serious failure. Isaac let personal affection and appetite override what God had said. How often do we do the same — allowing our likes, our comfort, or our stubbornness to steer us against what we know God desires?

The sad chain of events that follows in this chapter grows out of a whole family ignoring God and grasping for control in their own way. It is a reminder to hold God's word above our own preferences, especially in the decisions that matter most.

Before making an important decision, it is worth pausing to ask: Am I following what God has said, or simply what I want? Our affections are powerful, but they are not always right. God's word is the surer guide.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where might my preferences be pulling me against what God has said?
2. Do I hold God's word above my own likes and comfort?
3. In my biggest decisions, am I seeking God's will or my own?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from letting my preferences override Your word. Help me to honour what You have said, even when my own desires pull the other way. Amen.
